# Keywords, groups and workspace filters

A keyword is a term Rumoro watches, with a `kind` of `brand`, `competitor` or `topic`. Matching starts on the next collection run of each platform. `matching` rules decide what is stored, so a rejected post is never billed; `context` only changes the classifier's score. Workspace-wide rules live in the filters. Keywords belong to groups, so one workspace can keep separate customers or campaigns. A keyword costs $5 per month, debited daily from the prepaid balance, and every matched mention $0.008; a `402` means the balance can't cover it. Confirm with the user before deleting a keyword or a group.

Base URL `https://api.rumoro.dev`, `Authorization: Bearer $RUMORO_API_KEY` with each request, JSON in and out. Each endpoint names its `rumoro` CLI command for when the CLI is installed (rules/cli.md).

## Endpoints

### List keywords (`GET /v1/keywords`)

Returns the workspace's keywords with their match counts and polling status. With no parameters you get all keywords, latest first. `q` searches the term and context. `kind`, `status` and `platform` filter the list, `sort` orders it, and `limit` and `offset` page through it. `total` is the number of matching keywords before paging.

CLI command `rumoro keywords:list`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | query | string |  | Case-insensitive search in the term and context. |
| `groupId` | query | string[] or null |  | Keeps keywords in these groups only (grp_...). Repeat the parameter or separate values with commas. |
| `kind` | query | list of `brand`, `competitor`, `topic` |  | Keeps keywords of these kinds only (brand, competitor, topic). Repeat the parameter or separate values with commas. |
| `status` | query | list of `active`, `muted`, `paused`, `noisy`, `capped` |  | Keeps keywords in these states only (active, muted, paused, capped). Repeat the parameter or separate values with commas. |
| `platform` | query | list of `bluesky`, `hackernews`, `github`, `stackoverflow`, `devto`, `reddit`, `x`, `youtube`, `news`, `linkedin`, `tiktok`, `instagram`, `appstore`, `googleplay`, `trustpilot`, `googlemaps` |  | Keeps keywords that run on one of these platforms. That means the term is searched there, which is every platform when platforms is null. For appstore and googleplay it means an app from that store is in reviewSources. Repeat the parameter or separate values with commas. |
| `sort` | query | `newest`, `oldest`, `term`, `mentions`, `relevant`, `recent`, `lastMention` |  | newest puts the latest created first and oldest the earliest. term sorts A to Z. mentions puts the most matches first and relevant the most relevant matches. recent puts the most matches of the past 7 days first. lastMention puts the latest matched post first, with keywords that have none at the end. |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | How many to return, from 1 to 500. Leave it out to get all keywords after `offset`. |
| `offset` | query | integer or null |  | How many keywords to skip. |

Answers `200` with `data`, `total` (the keywords that match, with their total).

### Create a keyword (`POST /v1/keywords`)

Starts monitoring a word or phrase. Matching, scoring and delivery start with the next poll. A workspace with balance can have up to 500 keywords, each costing $5 a month, taken from the balance day by day. `matching` narrows what counts as a match, with required and excluded terms, excluded authors and case, before anything is stored, so rejected posts are never billed. `context` is a sentence only this keyword's classifier reads. `cap` limits matched mentions per month. At the cap the keyword stops matching until the 1st of next month (UTC) or until you raise the cap, and its daily charge continues.

CLI command `rumoro keywords:create`

JSON body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `term` | string | yes | The word or phrase to monitor. It matches as a whole phrase, ignoring case. |
| `kind` | `brand`, `competitor`, `topic` |  | brand is for your own names, competitor for a rival's, and topic for your market. Share of voice and segments use it. |
| `platforms` | list of `bluesky`, `hackernews`, `github`, `stackoverflow`, `devto`, `reddit`, `x`, `youtube`, `news`, `linkedin`, `tiktok`, `instagram` or null |  | The platforms to search for the term. Leave it out or send null for all platforms. An empty list searches nowhere, for a keyword that only collects reviews and so needs reviewSources. |
| `context` | string or null |  | Up to 300 characters the classifier reads for this keyword only, in addition to the company profile or the group's description. Say what the term means for you and what to ignore, for example "Basil is our deploy tool, not the herb." Null clears it. |
| `matching` | object |  | Fields you leave out stay as they are. An empty list clears a field. |
| `matching.requiredTerms` | string[] |  | Terms the post must contain as well. requiredMode says whether one or all of them must appear. An empty list sets no requirement. |
| `matching.requiredMode` | `any`, `all` |  | any needs one of the required terms in the post. all needs every one. |
| `matching.excludedTerms` | string[] |  | Posts that contain one of these terms are dropped. Put `*` at the start or end of a term as a wildcard, so deploy* matches deployment and *bot matches nightlybot. |
| `matching.excludedAuthors` | string[] |  | Authors whose posts this keyword ignores. Each entry is a profile or post link, @handle, u/name, Bluesky DID or display name. Entries are normalized the same way as an alert's muted authors. |
| `matching.caseSensitive` | boolean |  | When true, the term only matches in the exact case you typed, so RAG never matches rag. Defaults to false. |
| `cap` | object or null |  | Monthly limit on matched mentions. Omit or null means none. |
| `cap.mentions` | integer | yes | How many matched mentions the keyword may collect per calendar month (UTC). Every match counts, relevant or not, including a new keyword's look-back, since every match is billed. |
| `groupId` | string |  | The group to put it in (grp_...). Without it, the workspace's default group is used. Each group can hold a term only once. |
| `reviewSources` | object[] |  | Review pages for this keyword, at most 10 (App Store and Google Play apps, Trustpilot pages, Google Maps places). Every new review on them is a mention, whatever it says. Pages are read daily, per country on the app stores. A newly added page imports its last 30 days, up to 100 newest reviews per country, free and without instant alerts. Later reviews are billed like other mentions. |
| `reviewSources[].url` | string |  | Review page link, or send platform and id instead. Accepts App Store and Google Play app links (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/slack/id618783545, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.Slack), Trustpilot pages (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/slack.com) and Google Maps places (full or maps.app.goo.gl link). |
| `reviewSources[].platform` | `appstore`, `googleplay`, `trustpilot`, `googlemaps` |  | Where the reviews come from. appstore is the Apple App Store, googleplay is Google Play, trustpilot is a company's Trustpilot page and googlemaps is the Google reviews of a place. |
| `reviewSources[].id` | string |  | The platform's own id. On the App Store it is the number after "id" in the link, on Google Play the package name, on Trustpilot the company's domain (slack.com) and on Google Maps a Place ID (ChIJ...). |
| `reviewSources[].countries` | string[] |  | For App Store and Google Play. Up to 20 storefronts to read, as two-letter codes. Without it, the storefront in the link is used, or us. Each storefront adds one poll a day, and a review found in two storefronts is still one mention. Trustpilot and Google Maps have a single page and take no countries. |
| `reviewSources[].language` | string |  | For Google Play. The review language to read, such as en, es, de or pt-BR, since Google Play returns one language at a time. Without it, the link's hl is used, or en. |

Answers `201` with `id`, `term`, `kind`, `muted`, `pausedForBalance`, `pausedForNoise`, `pausedForCap`, `cap`, `group`, `platforms`, `reviewSources`, `context`, `matching`, `stats`, `polling`, `createdAt` (the new keyword).

### Get a keyword (`GET /v1/keywords/{id}`)

Returns one keyword with its matching rules, review pages, this month's cost and the polling status on each platform.

CLI command `rumoro keywords:get`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The keyword's id (kw_...). |

Answers `200` with `id`, `term`, `kind`, `muted`, `pausedForBalance`, `pausedForNoise`, `pausedForCap`, `cap`, `group`, `platforms`, `reviewSources`, `context`, `matching`, `stats`, `polling`, `createdAt` (the requested keyword).

### Update a keyword (`PATCH /v1/keywords/{id}`)

Mutes or unmutes the keyword, or changes its `kind`, platforms, classifier `context`, `matching` rules or monthly mention `cap`. Each rule field is optional and an empty list clears it. A null cap removes the cap, and a cap above this month's count resumes a capped keyword right away. New rules apply to mentions from the next poll on. Stored mentions stay as they are.

CLI command `rumoro keywords:update`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The keyword's id (kw_...). |

JSON body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `brand`, `competitor`, `topic` |  | New kind (brand, competitor or topic). |
| `muted` | boolean |  | Muting stops polling and matching. Existing mentions are kept. |
| `platforms` | list of `bluesky`, `hackernews`, `github`, `stackoverflow`, `devto`, `reddit`, `x`, `youtube`, `news`, `linkedin`, `tiktok`, `instagram` or null |  | Sets a new platform list. Null means all platforms. An empty list means none, which works when the keyword has reviewSources and only collects reviews. |
| `context` | string or null |  | Up to 300 characters the classifier reads for this keyword only, in addition to the company profile or the group's description. Say what the term means for you and what to ignore, for example "Basil is our deploy tool, not the herb." Null clears it. |
| `matching` | object |  | Fields you leave out stay as they are. An empty list clears a field. |
| `matching.requiredTerms` | string[] |  | Terms the post must contain as well. requiredMode says whether one or all of them must appear. An empty list sets no requirement. |
| `matching.requiredMode` | `any`, `all` |  | any needs one of the required terms in the post. all needs every one. |
| `matching.excludedTerms` | string[] |  | Posts that contain one of these terms are dropped. Put `*` at the start or end of a term as a wildcard, so deploy* matches deployment and *bot matches nightlybot. |
| `matching.excludedAuthors` | string[] |  | Authors whose posts this keyword ignores. Each entry is a profile or post link, @handle, u/name, Bluesky DID or display name. Entries are normalized the same way as an alert's muted authors. |
| `matching.caseSensitive` | boolean |  | When true, the term only matches in the exact case you typed, so RAG never matches rag. Defaults to false. |
| `cap` | object or null |  | Sets a new monthly mention cap, or null for no cap. A cap above this month's count resumes a capped keyword right away. A cap at or below the count pauses it. |
| `cap.mentions` | integer | yes | How many matched mentions the keyword may collect per calendar month (UTC). Every match counts, relevant or not, including a new keyword's look-back, since every match is billed. |
| `groupId` | string |  | Target group (grp_...). 409 if it already has this term. |
| `reviewSources` | object[] |  | Sets a new list of review pages for this keyword. An empty list disconnects them all, and their reviews are kept. A page or country you add gets the free 30-day look-back. Pages already listed are unchanged. |
| `reviewSources[].url` | string |  | Review page link, or send platform and id instead. Accepts App Store and Google Play app links (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/slack/id618783545, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.Slack), Trustpilot pages (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/slack.com) and Google Maps places (full or maps.app.goo.gl link). |
| `reviewSources[].platform` | `appstore`, `googleplay`, `trustpilot`, `googlemaps` |  | Where the reviews come from. appstore is the Apple App Store, googleplay is Google Play, trustpilot is a company's Trustpilot page and googlemaps is the Google reviews of a place. |
| `reviewSources[].id` | string |  | The platform's own id. On the App Store it is the number after "id" in the link, on Google Play the package name, on Trustpilot the company's domain (slack.com) and on Google Maps a Place ID (ChIJ...). |
| `reviewSources[].countries` | string[] |  | For App Store and Google Play. Up to 20 storefronts to read, as two-letter codes. Without it, the storefront in the link is used, or us. Each storefront adds one poll a day, and a review found in two storefronts is still one mention. Trustpilot and Google Maps have a single page and take no countries. |
| `reviewSources[].language` | string |  | For Google Play. The review language to read, such as en, es, de or pt-BR, since Google Play returns one language at a time. Without it, the link's hl is used, or en. |

Answers `200` with `id`, `term`, `kind`, `muted`, `pausedForBalance`, `pausedForNoise`, `pausedForCap`, `cap`, `group`, `platforms`, `reviewSources`, `context`, `matching`, `stats`, `polling`, `createdAt` (the keyword after the change).

### Delete a keyword (`DELETE /v1/keywords/{id}`)

Deletes the keyword with its matches. A post that another keyword also matched is kept.

CLI command `rumoro keywords:delete`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The keyword's id (kw_...). |

Answers `204` (done).

### Check a keyword's health (`GET /v1/keywords/{id}/health`)

Checks whether the keyword earns its cost over `range` (default 30d). Returns a status (healthy, noisy, quiet, capped, paused or new) with plain-word reasons, numbers by platform and week, cost, the words and authors behind the noise, and suggestions. Send a suggestion's `patch` unchanged to PATCH /v1/keywords/{id}. Its effect comes from replaying the matcher's rules on the window's posts. `ai=true` adds a model-written context (cached a day, up to 20 model calls an hour per workspace). Read only and never billed. Reports are cached 5 minutes and rebuilt after a keyword change. Up to 30 reads a minute per workspace.

CLI command `rumoro keywords:health`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The keyword's id (kw_...). |
| `range` | query | `7d`, `30d`, `90d` |  | How many UTC days back from today to read, by match time. One of 7d, 30d or 90d, 30d by default. |
| `ai` | query | boolean |  | true also asks a language model to rewrite the context. The answer is cached for a day per keyword and window, with at most 20 model calls an hour per workspace. With the default false, all suggestions come from the rules only. |

Answers `200` with `keyword`, `window`, `status`, `reasons`, `stats`, `sample`, `noiseTerms`, `noiseAuthors`, `suggestions`, `ai`, `generatedAt` (the health report for the keyword).

### Get the workspace filters (`GET /v1/filters`)

Returns the workspace noise rules, applied to every keyword before a mention is stored. They exclude terms, authors and GitHub repositories, and allow or block subreddits. Rejected posts are never classified, sent or billed. Keywords add their own `matching` rules on top.

CLI command `rumoro filters:get`

Answers `200` with `excludedTerms`, `excludedAuthors`, `excludedRepos`, `subreddits`, `updatedAt` (the workspace's filters).

### Update the workspace filters (`PATCH /v1/filters`)

Sets new values for any of the lists. A list you leave out stays as it is, and an empty list clears it. Rumoro normalizes each entry. Terms become lowercase, authors profile links or plain names, repositories owner/name, and subreddits lose the r/. New mentions follow the change within a minute. Stored mentions stay as they are.

CLI command `rumoro filters:update`

JSON body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `excludedTerms` | string[] |  | Sets a new list. An empty list clears it. |
| `excludedAuthors` | string[] |  | Sets a new list. An empty list clears it. |
| `excludedRepos` | string[] |  | Sets a new list. An empty list clears it. |
| `subreddits` | object |  | Applies to Reddit only. A list you leave out stays as it is. |
| `subreddits.only` | string[] |  | Sets a new list of allowed subreddits. An empty list clears it. |
| `subreddits.excluded` | string[] |  | Sets a new list of blocked subreddits. An empty list clears it. |

Answers `200` with `excludedTerms`, `excludedAuthors`, `excludedRepos`, `subreddits`, `updatedAt` (the filters after the change).

### List groups (`GET /v1/groups`)

Returns the workspace's keyword groups, the default group first and then the oldest. Groups organize keywords, for example by client, campaign or product. Every keyword is in one group, a group can hold a term once, and GET /v1/usage/breakdown?by=group shows each group's cost. `externalId` looks a group up by your own id.

CLI command `rumoro groups:list`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `externalId` | query | string |  | Filters to the one group whose externalId matches exactly. |

Answers `200` with `data` (the workspace's groups).

### Create a group (`POST /v1/groups`)

Creates a keyword group. `name` must be unique in the workspace. `externalId` is optional and also unique. It is your own id, such as a client id, so you can find the group without storing ours. `context` is optional. It is a company description for this group, which the classifier reads instead of the workspace profile for the group's keywords. Then send the group's id as `groupId` when you create a keyword.

CLI command `rumoro groups:create`

JSON body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | The group's name, such as a client, campaign or product. Must be unique in the workspace. |
| `externalId` | string or null |  | An id from your own system, such as a client id. Must be unique in the workspace. Find the group with GET /v1/groups?externalId=. |
| `context` | string or null |  | Up to 4000 characters the classifier treats as "the company" for this group's keywords. It fully replaces the workspace profile, including its relevance guidelines and competitors. Describe the business, what it sells and to whom, what it is not, and any rule for this group, such as "ignore job posts". With one group per client, use the client's description. Null means the workspace profile is used. |

Answers `201` (the group that was created).

### Get a group (`GET /v1/groups/{id}`)

Returns one keyword group with its external id and keyword counts.

CLI command `rumoro groups:get`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The group's id (grp_...). |

Answers `200` (the requested group).

### Update a group (`PATCH /v1/groups/{id}`)

Changes a group's name, your `externalId` for it or its company description in `context`. Null clears externalId. Null clears context too, so the workspace profile applies again. New mentions use the new context right away, and older ones are not scored again. You can rename the default group, but it takes no description, because it is the workspace itself and uses the company profile.

CLI command `rumoro groups:update`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The group's id (grp_...). |

JSON body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | The group's name, such as a client, campaign or product. Must be unique in the workspace. |
| `externalId` | string or null |  | Sets a new external id. Null removes it. |
| `context` | string or null |  | Sets a new company description for the group. Null removes it, and the workspace profile applies again. New mentions use it right away, and older ones are not scored again. The default group cannot have one (400 default_group_context), because it is the workspace itself and uses the profile. |

Answers `200` (the group after the change).

### Delete a group (`DELETE /v1/groups/{id}`)

Deletes the group and all of its keywords, each as DELETE /v1/keywords/{id} would. Their mentions are deleted too, alert rules that named them are updated, and past charges stay in the usage record. Read the group first, since `stats.keywords` tells you how many keywords will be deleted. Only non-default groups can be deleted.

CLI command `rumoro groups:delete`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The group's id (grp_...). |

Answers `204` (the group and its keywords were removed).
